title: Manifest
description: A kit manifest. It tells the generic bridge what to read and where to find it (docs/architecture.md §6.1).

tool_prefix.description: Prefix for this kit's MCP tools, which are named `{tool_prefix}_{verb}_{noun}` (§10.1). Lowercase snake_case, `[a-z0-9_]` only. At most 60 characters, so that a tool name fits in 64.

flavors.description: The single registry of per-flavor config, keyed by flavor (§6.4). Ingest rejects a payload whose flavor is not a key here (§8.3).

root.title: Root
root.description: How the bridge finds the game's install folder.

locate.description: An ordered chain. The bridge tries each entry in turn; if none resolves, it prompts the user.

verify.description: A glob, relative to root, that must match under a candidate root for it to count. No variables.

path.description: A candidate install folder. Globs allowed. The only variables are `{PROGRAM_FILES_X86}` and `{HOME}`; no other `{` or `}` is allowed.

prompt.description: The title of the folder picker the bridge shows the user.

adapter.title: Adapter
adapter.description: The in-game adapter. Omit it for adapter-less kits.

install.description: Where the bridge installs the adapter, relative to root. Globs expand to each existing match. No variables.

process.description: Globs for the game's process names. The bridge applies adapter updates only while none is running (§7).

source.title: Source
source.description: One kind of thing the bridge reads. Each file its path matches is a source instance.

id.description: The source's ID, sent as `source_id` at ingest (§8.3).

type.description: Only `file` is implemented. New types are added to this enum.

path.description: Relative to root. Globs allowed; the bridge watches every match. No variables.

search.description: The flavor's search scope (§12). Each entry is a URL prefix with a scheme, a host, and a path that starts with `/`, not a bare domain. Empty means no vetted sources yet.

relativePath.description: A path relative to root. Globs allowed. No variables, so no `{` or `}`.
